Sierpe is linked to the river of the same name in southern Costa Rica. Boat journeys start here through mangrove-lined waterways toward the Pacific coast. The river landscape reveals natural areas that differ from the country's highland forests and volcanic regions.

From the boat, you can see the riverbanks, mangrove thickets, and bends in the channel. Sierpe connects the road portion of a journey with sea and forest routes in the south, including excursions to the Corcovado area. The appeal lies in the changing surroundings: from settlement and pier to river channels and coast.

Sierra de la Ventana is one of the centers of mountain recreation in Tornquist municipality. Instead of the flat horizon of the pampas, you find rocky slopes, valleys, and trails of the Ventania range.

We suggest stopping here for a nature break between cities and professional visits. You can spend time walking and set aside a separate day for Ernesto Tornquist Park. We'll choose a walking route suited to participants' fitness and available conditions. This kind of rest complements a busy business trip: nature in the morning, followed by free time in a small resort town after returning.

The Siloli Desert, a stop on high-altitude journeys through Bolivia, lies along routes between the Uyuni Salt Flat and the lagoons of the Lípez region. Travelers encounter wide-open desert landscapes and rock formations here.

One of the sights on the itinerary, the Stone Tree, reveals the unusual shapes of local rocks. From Siloli, the route continues toward the Red Lagoon and the geothermal areas of the highlands.

Soberanía lies near the Panama Canal and preserves tracts of tropical forest. In this part of the country, nature sits particularly close to the engineered passage between the oceans. Forest walks reveal the vegetation and offer opportunities to watch birds.

Gamboa and river trips along the Chagres are associated with this area. Exploring the park adds a natural dimension to a visit to the canal, shifting attention from large ships to the forest and its wildlife. Soberanía makes an interesting stop near the capital or part of a longer journey through Panama.
